rulings.challenge_claim: The decisive closing-seam ground - a person and addressee shift between Isa.25.5 and Isa.25.6 - is asserted from the English rendering with no Hebrew form quoted on either side of the seam, and the front seam is crossed undisclosed by the exalt/height root that the preceding unit's own object supplies; separately the rationale points at a governing planning document as authority for the site.
rulings.grounds: Two of the three arms hold, the third does not, and the severity is set too low. ARM 1 (upheld): the row's whole closing warrant is a person/addressee shift at the Isa.25.5 | Isa.25.6 seam, and the row's only pointed splice sits at oshb:Isa.25.1 - no Hebrew is quoted on either side of the seam it calls decisive. The claim is byte-TRUE and unengaged: second-person address runs unbroken through the span (oshb:Isa.25.2 שַׂ֤מְתָּ, oshb:Isa.25.3 יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ and יִירָאֽוּךָ, oshb:Isa.25.4 הָיִ֨יתָ, all byte tier) and closes on תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier), which the English reads “you will bring down the noise of strangers” (web:Isa.25.5), while oshb:Isa.25.6 opens וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (byte tier), putting the divine name in as explicit third-person subject - “Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast” (web:Isa.25.6). The engagement mandate for boundary-relevant Hebrew claims is breached at the row's own decisive edge. ARM 2 (upheld, and under-weighted by the challenge): the rationale asserts its site as 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' - a governing-document authority claim inside boundary_rationale, which the register bar forbids in row prose in every field. The challenge relegates this to a trailing sentence; it is in fact the row's most concrete and most mechanically curable defect - and the same breach class at Isa.25.10-Isa.25.12 in this cluster is carried at medium. ARM 3 (refuted as a defect, retained as an observation): the exalt/height link between אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.25.1, byte tier) and צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier) is NOT byte-true and not even a contiguous consonantal match - swept per attested spelling the mem-prefixed spelling stands at 13 verses book-wide and 4 in chs 23-27 (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Isa.24.4, oshb:Isa.24.18, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.26.5) and the bare spelling at 7 book-wide and 2 here (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.23.4, oshb:Isa.25.1); the challenge's own digits verify exactly. The cross-seam cohesion rule binds byte-true devices straddling a row's own seam; a root-level echo at two different spellings is a disclosure courtesy, not a rule breach, and cannot carry severity on its own. Mark layer is correct as both primaries say: PE after oshb:Isa.24.23 and PE after oshb:Isa.25.5 bracket the span exactly, types unconflated, single-witness disclosed, and no mark falls inside Isa.25.1-Isa.25.5 (tier-3, absence not used either way).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: (a) delete the clause 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' outright - the site must be argued from this row's own bytes and nothing else; (b) add pointed splices on BOTH sides of the closing seam - תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier) and וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier) - with the form-class label held as a byte-checkable claim, since no morphology layer is available. Optional in device_notes: one sentence disclosing the exalt/height echo to oshb:Isa.24.21 as root-level per attested spelling, explicitly NOT byte-identical. No boundary change is proposed and none is needed. TESTS the cure must pass: the register scan finds no governing-document or planning-file reference in any field; every Hebrew run in the row re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse; the closing-seam sentence names a tier for every form it labels.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row makes a demonstrative mountain-phrase its identifying frame without disclosing that the same phrase recurs on the far side of its own closing seam and without naming the tier at which the far site matches; and the divine-name object at Isa.25.8 goes unnamed while only the hosts-title is engaged.
rulings.grounds: The tier finding is exactly right and is the real defect; the 'runs through' framing and the divine-name arm are not. VERIFIED: בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה stands byte-identical at oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier) and recurs at oshb:Isa.25.10 as בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה - the accents differ, so the third site matches only at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses at those tiers, 2 at byte). The row makes the phrase its identifying frame ('matching בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier)') and discloses neither the in-span repetition at oshb:Isa.25.7 nor the recurrence past its own closing edge nor the tier drop at that far site - and the campaign standard requires the tier named on EVERY recurrence claim. CORRECTION to the framing: the phrase does not 'run oshb:Isa.25.6 through oshb:Isa.25.10'. oshb:Isa.25.8 and oshb:Isa.25.9 carry no occurrence at any tier, so the signal is three sites with a two-verse gap, and no site sits on either side of the row's own 25:8 | 25:9 seam. It argues a mountain-motif band reaching two verses past the row's close, which is a real disclosure obligation, but it is weaker than a device straddling the seam itself. REFUTED arm: אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה does stand byte-true at oshb:Isa.25.8, but the row makes no divine-name count claim anywhere - it names a title as span texture - and the count-object discipline bites on digits and swept objects, not on an obligation to enumerate every title present in a span. This is an observation, not a defect. Sound as the challenge says: בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֨וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח (oshb:Isa.25.8, byte tier) answers the waw-prefixed verb opening oshb:Isa.25.7 in-span; the back-seam opener וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.25.9) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte AND skeleton tier); PE after oshb:Isa.25.5 and PE after oshb:Isa.25.8 match the inventory under the right type.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add one sentence disclosing that the row's identifying mountain-phrase repeats in-span at oshb:Isa.25.7 (byte tier) and recurs beyond the row's close at oshb:Isa.25.10 at accent_stripped / skeleton tier only (sweep: 2 verses byte, 3 verses accent_stripped), and state that the motif band is not treated as a boundary driver. Do NOT restate it as a continuous run and do not add a divine-name enumeration. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the recurrence sentence names a tier and a digit with its unit; a byte-tier sweep of the cited phrase returns exactly oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 and an accent_stripped sweep adds oshb:Isa.25.10 and nothing else.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the applied unit_type is given to a projected communal confession without the one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category rule requires. OL: a one-verse row is cut out of the middle of a three-verse anaphoric chain with no disclosure at either edge, and its back seam is crossed by a causal particle that subordinates the following clause to this verse.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one - LF's is a category-disclosure defect in device_notes, OL's is a seam-engagement defect in boundary_rationale. LF UPHELD as written: the applied value's operative line is the promise/comfort oracle, and this row's own literature_type_guess calls the verse a communal confession formula - quoted retrospective acclamation by the people (וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא, oshb:Isa.25.9, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse). The operative-category law admits any closed-vocabulary value wherever the row's bytes carry that form, but ONLY with a one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes; this row's device_notes carries none, while the Isa.26.7-Isa.26.19 row in this cluster does supply one for the same law. Refinement of LF's framing only: the trigger is the mismatch with the operative DESCRIPTION, not absence from the enumerated example list (the adjacent Isa.25.6-Isa.25.8 row is equally off-list yet squarely promise/comfort and needs no disclosure), and LF's suggested sung-praise alternative is weak - the verse is reported speech, not a sung unit - so the defect is the missing sentence, not the label chosen. OL REFINED. Its second arm is byte-true and is the stronger finding: oshb:Isa.25.10 opens כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ (byte tier), a causal particle binding the following clause back across this row's closing edge, and the rationale argues that cut only forward (a subject narrowing to a named foreign power at 25:10) without ever engaging the particle pointing backward. Its first arm is materially misframed: the mountain-phrase sites are oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 (byte) and oshb:Isa.25.10 (accent_stripped / skeleton), so this row is NOT 'precisely the single verse wedged between the second and third sites' - oshb:Isa.25.8 lies between them too, and the phrase occurs nowhere inside this row. The chain brackets a two-verse gap spanning two rows; it does not isolate this one. Correct in both packets: PE after oshb:Isa.25.8 is cited under the right type as single-witness, and the inventory records no mark after oshb:Isa.25.9, as the row implies.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure for the applied unit_type, arguing the value from this verse's own bytes (quoted future acclamation under its own reported-speech frame) - one sentence, no label change proposed. (2) boundary_rationale: engage the closing seam in BOTH directions - splice כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ (oshb:Isa.25.10, byte tier) and state why the causal particle does not bind Isa.25.10 into this verse's unit, or record the rival honestly and re-check the confidence band. Do NOT write the mountain-phrase chain up as a continuous run; if it is disclosed, cite it as sites with tiers. No respan is proposed here; any actual boundary change is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. TESTS: device_notes contains exactly one deviation sentence naming the applied value; the closing-seam sentence carries a pointed splice from oshb:Isa.25.10 that re-collates at byte tier; no sentence asserts a continuous phrase run across oshb:Isa.25.8-Isa.25.9.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's own notes name the shared staged verification apparatus directly ('per the toolkit's fold guidance'), a barred staged-file reference in row prose. OL: the layout datum the row discloses is misdescribed - the English continuation paragraph is a mid-verse break inside Isa.25.10 at the Moab pivot, not a fold onto Isa.25.9 - and the byte-identical clause pair straddling the row's closing seam is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT defects sitting in the same two fields. LF UPHELD: device_notes reads 'per the toolkit's fold guidance', naming the shared staged verification apparatus in row prose - the register bar forbids tool and staged-file names in EVERY field, and the sentence adds nothing the fold disclosure does not already carry. OL UPHELD, and byte-confirmed from the source layout rather than from the derived map: the English opens a paragraph BEFORE web:Isa.25.9, and web:Isa.25.10 carries its single continuation paragraph INTERNALLY, immediately before “Moab will be trodden down in his place” (web:Isa.25.10) - i.e. the break lands exactly on the Moab pivot the row uses as its own content ground. The row states the opposite twice (a fold 'onto' 25:9 in boundary_rationale, a fold 'linking' 25:9 and 25:10 in device_notes) and its strongest_rejected_alternative rests on that description, so a tier-4 datum that can never drive is nonetheless misreported in a load-bearing field, and the row argues against a layout signal that does not exist while ignoring the one that does. OL's cross-seam arm also verifies: עַד עָפָֽר is BYTE-identical at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5), one on each side of this row's back edge; הֵשַׁ֥ח / הֵשַׁח֙ match at accent_stripped tier at those same two verses (the further skeleton hit at oshb:Isa.25.11 is the swimming lexeme, a different object, as the challenge says); and מִשְׂגַּ֣ב / נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה share the sgv skeleton, which stands at 9 verses book-wide with only these two in chs 23-27. That is a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam and it is answered nowhere. NEW FINDING (cross-check): the LF packet verified this same fold as 'confirmed against the staged verse map' and accepted the row's description - the existence digit was reproduced with the wrong count-object, which is the defect class the peer round exists to catch. Correct as written in the row: the opening splice properly includes the governing particle כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ; the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.25.10 is disclosed single-witness and the quotation stops well before the staged doubled pair; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.25.12 matches the inventory under the right type.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes: delete the clause 'per the toolkit's fold guidance' - the fold disclosure stands on its own. (2) boundary_rationale AND device_notes: restate the layout datum correctly in one place only - the continuation paragraph is INTERNAL to web:Isa.25.10, falling before “Moab will be trodden down in his place” (web:Isa.25.10) - and keep it labelled tier-4 and non-driving; then rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative so it no longer rests on the false 'fold onto Isa.25.9' description (the content pivot to the named foreign power already carries it). (3) SEAM-PAIR EDIT, one edit across this row and the following one: disclose the עַד עָפָֽר bracket as byte-identical at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.25.12 | oshb:Isa.26.5) with the heshach pair named at accent_stripped tier and the sgv pair at skeleton tier, and say why it does not bind the two rows into one. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the register scan finds no tool or staged-file name in any field; the layout sentence, read against the source paragraphing, places the break inside web:Isa.25.10 and not at the 25:9 | 25:10 join; a byte-tier sweep of the cited two-word run returns exactly oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5; the same disclosure appears on both sides of the seam pair.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing seam and the rejected alternative both rest solely on the English translation's quotation punctuation, which has no counterpart in the Hebrew, and the row's two named devices are asserted without a single Hebrew form quoted for either; the front seam is also crossed undisclosed by a byte-identical clause pair.
rulings.grounds: Upheld at high, and the severity is right because this is a DRIVER defect, not a disclosure gap. The row's only pointed splice is at oshb:Isa.26.1. Its closing edge is carried entirely by where the translation's closing quotation mark falls at web:Isa.26.6, plus the absence of further quotation punctuation before web:Isa.27.2, and strongest_rejected_alternative repeats that same punctuation ground and nothing else. The punctuation FACT checks out (curly-quote scan over the staged English: an opening mark at web:Isa.26.1, a closing mark at web:Isa.26.6, and zero quotation characters anywhere in web:Isa.26.7-web:Isa.26.21 before the next opening mark at web:Isa.27.2), so the challenge is not about a wrong digit - it is that translation punctuation is a tier-4 rendering artifact with no counterpart at any tier in the pointed bytes, and tier-4 is never boundary evidence. The row therefore has NO admissible warrant for its back edge, and the co-primary packet supported this row while itself labelling the driver tier-4 - an internal inconsistency that does not survive the bytes. Hebrew grounds for the same seam exist unused, exactly as the challenge says: oshb:Isa.26.7 opens אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier) on a fresh gnomic subject. Unquoted-form gaps verified: the imperative at 26:4 stands in the bytes as בִּטְח֥וּ (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier) and is quoted only in English; the short-form divine title stands as בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier), and although the row's digit is right (the short form is one of exactly three book-wide sites - oshb:Isa.12.2, oshb:Isa.26.4, oshb:Isa.38.11), a form-class label and a divine-title object are byte-checkable claims and owe the bytes, not the rendering. Front seam undisclosed, verified: עַד עָפָֽר is byte-identical at exactly oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), one site immediately outside this row and one inside it. Back-seam catchword verified too: the righteous-one term stands at oshb:Isa.26.2 and twice at oshb:Isa.26.7, and its lamed-prefixed spelling at exactly two verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.24.16, oshb:Isa.26.7). Correct as written: SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.25.12 is cited under the right type, and the inventory records no parashah mark inside Isa.26.1-Isa.26.6, as the row claims (tier-3, single-witness, absence not used as counterevidence).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the punctuation-only closing warrant with a byte arm - splice אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.26.7, byte tier) and argue the fresh gnomic subject at the 26:6 | 26:7 seam; the English quotation punctuation may remain ONLY as an explicitly tier-4, non-driving corroboration sentence. strongest_rejected_alternative must be rewritten on the same byte ground - a replacement warrant has to pass the test that killed the original, so a rejected alternative resting on punctuation alone fails again. Add pointed splices for both named devices: בִּטְח֥וּ (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier) for the imperative, with the form-class held as a byte-checkable claim, and בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier) for the short-form title, keeping the existing 3-verse digit and naming its object. Add the seam-pair front-edge disclosure of the עַד עָפָֽר bracket (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) as ONE edit shared with the preceding row. No boundary change is proposed: the span may well be right, but its warrant must be re-cut. TESTS: no field states or implies that translation punctuation sets an edge; every device claim in the row carries a pointed splice re-collating at byte tier against its cited verse; strongest_rejected_ alternative names a Hebrew form and a tier; the cross-seam bracket is disclosed identically on both sides of the seam pair.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row quotes web:Isa.26.20 as its own close-boundary evidence without disclosing that the underlying Masoretic verse is ketiv/qere-bearing. OL: the stated reason for rejecting the internal marks is byte-false at the first of them, the row's own closing criterion is already satisfied inside its last verse, and it quotes the doubled ketiv/qere verse at its back seam with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row.
rulings.grounds: The two packets OVERLAP on one arm (the undisclosed ketiv/qere) and OL adds two arms the other packet did not reach. All three are real. ARM 1, OL only, and the reason the severity is high: strongest_rejected_alternative rejects both internal marks on the ground that 'neither break carries an addressee or person shift' and that the second-person appeal 'persists in the same voice from Isa.26.7 through Isa.26.19'. The bytes contradict that at the first mark. The 2ms pronominal-suffix grapheme occurs twice in oshb:Isa.26.9, ZERO times in oshb:Isa.26.10, and twice in oshb:Isa.26.11 (count: 2 / 0 / 2, graphemic, over the pointed bytes); oshb:Isa.26.10 closes on גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה - “will not see Yahweh’s majesty.” (web:Isa.26.10) - a third-person reference to the divine name, and oshb:Isa.26.11 opens verse-initially יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ (byte tier), resuming direct address. The SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.10 therefore sits exactly where second-person address resumes - the one place in the span where the row's own stated criterion is met - so a tier-3 mark is overridden on a ground that is false at that mark. The row's blanket claim is nevertheless TRUE at the second mark: 2ms address stands on both sides of the break after oshb:Isa.26.11 (oshb:Isa.26.12 פָּעַ֥לְתָּ, oshb:Isa.26.13 זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ and בְּךָ֖, byte tier), and the challenge correctly scoped its finding to 'the first one'. Note the marks stay tier-3 weak and cannot drive an edge in either direction; the defect is the false reason, not the decision. ARM 2, OL only, correctly HELD rather than asserted: the closing criterion (a voice commanding the community, said to begin only at 26:20) is already present inside the row's final verse - הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier; the two runs are each unique in the book, sweep: 1 verse each), rendered “Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust” (web:Isa.26.19). With no morphology layer staged this is a form-class reading, and the challenge flags it as held; the point stands as stated - the criterion as written does not separate 26:19 from 26:20. ARM 3, BOTH packets, same defect: the row quotes “Come, my people, enter into your rooms” (web:Isa.26.20) as its close-boundary evidence with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere, while oshb:Isa.26.20 carries TWO notes staged as the doubled pairs דלתיך דְּלָתְךָ֖ and יעבור יַעֲבָר (single-witness); the adjacent row quoting the same verse does disclose both. The machine arm agrees - the citation sweep raises a ketiv/qere-versus-WEB-quote warning on this row and on no other row in the assignment. NEW FINDING neither packet reached: the variant is LOAD-BEARING for the quoted evidence, not merely adjacent to it. The English clause the row leans on renders “shut your doors behind you” (web:Isa.26.20) in the plural, aligning with the ketiv spelling דלתיך against the qere דְּלָתְךָ֖, and “until the indignation is past” (web:Isa.26.20) sits on the second note; held as a rendering-alignment observation, since no morphology layer is staged. Correct as written: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים and the resurrection splice both re-collate at byte tier in their cited verses, and the SAMEKH marks after oshb:Isa.26.10, oshb:Isa.26.11 and oshb:Isa.26.19 are all disclosed under the right type as single-witness.
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite so the stated ground is byte-true. It must concede the person shift at the break after oshb:Isa.26.10 - splice גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.26.10) and יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.26.11), both byte tier - and then argue the unit holds across it on some other tier-1 ground, or record the rival and re-check the confidence band; the blanket 'neither break carries an addressee or person shift' sentence cannot survive. Keep the marks explicitly tier-3 weak and non-driving. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing criterion so it distinguishes oshb:Isa.26.19 from oshb:Isa.26.20 - splice הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier), name the form-class as a byte-checkable claim, and state what separates the two verses beyond 'a voice commanding the community'. (3) SEAM-PAIR EDIT with the following row, one edit: add the ketiv/qere disclosure for oshb:Isa.26.20 (two notes, single-witness, quotation stopping before both staged pairs) AND note that the English clause quoted renders the plural, aligning with the ketiv - or stop quoting that clause. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the citation sweep's ketiv/qere-versus-WEB-quote warning no longer fires on this row; a 2ms-suffix grapheme count over oshb:Isa.26.9 / 26.10 / 26.11 returns 2 / 0 / 2 and the rewritten sentence agrees with it; every form-class label in the row is held or byte-shown; the same ketiv/qere disclosure appears on both sides of the seam pair.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing-seam ground names a frame formula in the next verse without ever quoting it, and the root repetition that hooks Isa.26.21 straight into Isa.27.1 across that seam is undisclosed; the front-edge criterion is also already present one verse earlier.
rulings.grounds: The engagement arm is upheld; the 'nowhere answered' framing of the cohesion arm is overstated and the tier is not what the wording implies. UPHELD: the row's closing edge rests wholly on a frame formula it attributes to the next verse and never quotes - and the row carries no oshb: reference for that verse at all, only web:Isa.27.1. The claim is true (oshb:Isa.27.1 does open verse-initially בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא, byte tier), but a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim with no pointed splice breaches the engagement mandate at the row's own decisive edge, and the seam-pair partner quotes the very same onset byte-true - the two sides of one seam are inconsistent. REFINED, cohesion arm: the hook is real but weaker and differently tiered than stated. This row's closing word is לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and the next verse continues יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier); the two forms are NOT byte-identical to each other - they share the consonantal skeleton only, which stands at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), while the fuller construction the challenge cites stands at exactly 3 verses at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.23.17, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.27.1), reopening the frame that opened this cluster at יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier). And the row does not leave the continuity wholly unanswered: its rationale states in terms that the verse 'continues without a further addressee change into the leviathan judgment of Isa.27.1' and rests the cut on the fresh formula plus the mark layer. What is missing is the Hebrew-level catchword and its tier, not the acknowledgement. The challenge's front-edge point verifies and is correctly held as a form-class reading: הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier) already reverses the direction of address one verse before the row opens, so the row's distinguishing criterion does not by itself separate the two verses. Correct as written and worth recording: the ketiv/qere handling here is exact - the splice stops at וּֽסְגֹ֥ר, before both staged pairs, with the doubling disclosed single-witness; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.19 and after oshb:Isa.26.21 are cited under the right type.

rulings.grounds: Both arms point at something real; the first names the wrong count-object and the second reaches past this row's own burden. ARM 1, REFINED - the object is blended. The three sites verify in the bytes: לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21), יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1) and פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.3), all byte tier in their cited verses, with the root skeleton at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses) exactly as the challenge says. But calling all three 'a divine-visitation chain' blends two speech-roles into one swept object, which the count-discipline bars: at oshb:Isa.26.21 and oshb:Isa.27.1 the visiting agent is the divine name itself, while oshb:Isa.27.3 is a negative-purpose clause inside first-person divine speech in which the speaker is the vineyard's KEEPER and the visiting agent is someone else - “Lest anyone damage it” (web:Isa.27.3). CORRECTED FINDING, and it is sharper than the original at the back edge: יִפְקֹ֣ד is BYTE-identical at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3), so a byte-true lexical recurrence does cross this row's closing edge and is undisclosed - but it must be cited as that lexical form, not as a visitation chain. At the front edge the link to לִפְקֹ֛ד is skeleton-level only, not byte. The 'straddling BOTH edges' wording also skips that oshb:Isa.27.2 carries no occurrence at any tier. The formula is also not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine, so its discriminating power is exactly the thing the row leaves unquantified - and the very next verse opens the same formula at accent_stripped tier (בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא, oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier in its own verse; the two openers differ in their accents, so they are NOT byte-identical to each other), which is the row's own seam.
